nodes.content: Develop a learned plasma fluid closure that recovers collisionless plasma echoes while preserving energy under unseen forcing histories.
requirements: Predict echo amplitudes within 10% of Vlasov–Poisson reference values on held-out forcing histories.
Keep unforced total energy drift below 0.1% over 100 plasma periods.

nodes.content: Use 64 Hermite memory modes, skew-symmetric moment coupling, and discrete-gradient time stepping to recover echoes while conserving unforced energy.
Can 64 Hermite modes retain phase-mixed information across unseen forcing delays without compromising discrete-gradient energy conservation?
Across held-out forcing delays, 64 Hermite modes should yield ≤10% echo-amplitude error and <0.1% unforced energy drift over 100 periods.
Generate Vlasov–Poisson two-pulse trajectories, train the 64-mode closure, then evaluate held-out delay echo errors and 100-period energy drift.
Run EchoDelay-v1: train on 2–8-period pulse separations; test 9–12-period delays against Vlasov–Poisson echoes and 100-period unforced energy drift.
EchoDelay-v1 yielded 8.6% maximum echo-amplitude error at 9–12-period delays and 0.06% unforced energy drift after 100 periods.
Retain the 64-mode closure for broader forcing-history validation; EchoDelay-v1 met both echo-error and energy-drift thresholds.
Validate the retained 64-mode closure on EchoHistory-v2’s unseen three-pulse and chirped drives, measuring echo error and post-drive energy drift.
Run EchoHistory-v2 on 200 unseen three-pulse and chirped histories against Vlasov–Poisson; measure echo-amplitude error and 100-period post-drive energy drift.
EchoHistory-v2 benchmark bundle containing 200 paired closure and Vlasov–Poisson trajectories, per-history echo-amplitude errors, and 100-period post-drive energy traces.
Analyze EchoHistory-v2’s paired trajectories, computing maximum echo-amplitude error separately for three-pulse and chirped histories and 100-period post-drive energy drift.
EchoHistory-v2 maximum echo errors were 8.9% (three-pulse) and 9.5% (chirped); unforced post-drive energy drift was 0.08% over 100 periods.
At 16–24-period pulse delays, high-mode reflection will push echo error above 10% while energy drift remains below 0.1%.
Run EchoDelay-Long across 16–24-period delays; measure Vlasov–Poisson echo error, mode-63 spectral pileup, and 100-period unforced energy drift.
EchoDelay-Long showed 9.8% maximum echo error, mode-63 energy below 0.2% of Hermite energy, and 0.09% unforced drift.
Does the 64-mode closure retain accurate difference-wavenumber echoes for unseen pulse pairs with k₂/k₁ between 1.5 and 2.5?
Run EchoK-v1 on unseen pulse pairs with k₂/k₁=1.5–2.5; compare difference-wavenumber echo-amplitude errors against Vlasov–Poisson.
EchoK-v1 benchmark table pairing Vlasov–Poisson and closure difference-wavenumber echo amplitudes, with per-ratio errors for k₂/k₁=1.5–2.5.
Train a port-Hamiltonian closure with oscillatory memory kernels and discrete-gradient stepping to reconstruct echoes while conserving unforced energy.
Can port-Hamiltonian oscillatory memory retain cross-wavenumber phase correlations through unseen pulse sequences while conserving unforced total energy?
A 32-pole port-Hamiltonian memory closure will achieve ≤10% unseen cross-wavenumber echo error and <0.1% unforced energy drift over 100 periods.
Fit 32-pole port-Hamiltonian memory on training pulses; score EchoK-v1 cross-wavenumber errors and 100-period unforced energy drift.
EchoK-v1’s 32-pole closure reached 14.2% maximum echo error at k₂/k₁=2.5, despite 0.04% unforced energy drift.
Antisymmetric cross-wavenumber coupling in the 32-pole memory should yield ≤10% EchoK-v1 error and <0.1% unforced drift over 100 periods.
Implement antisymmetric cross-wavenumber coupling in the 32-pole closure; rerun EchoK-v1 and measure maximum echo error and 100-period energy drift.
With antisymmetric coupling, EchoK-v1 maximum echo error fell from 14.2% to 8.7%; unforced energy drift was 0.05% over 100 periods.
Advance both closures to matched joint-history benchmarking: the 64-mode closure passed EchoHistory-v2; coupled 32-pole memory passed EchoK-v1.
Benchmark both closures on EchoJoint-v1 held-out chirped, three-pulse, cross-wavenumber histories; compare echo errors and 100-period unforced energy drift.
Run both closures on EchoJoint-v1 mixed-drive histories; measure echo-amplitude error against Vlasov–Poisson and 100-period unforced energy drift.
EchoJoint-v1 report containing paired Vlasov–Poisson and closure echo amplitudes by mixed-drive history, plus 100-period unforced energy traces.
Compute both closures’ worst-case echo errors and energy drift from EchoJoint-v1; compare 64-mode results with EchoHistory-v2.
EchoJoint-v1: 64-mode echo error reached 13.4% versus EchoHistory-v2’s 9.5%; coupled 32-pole achieved 8.8% error and 0.06% unforced 100-period drift.
Audit EchoJoint-v1 worst-case histories for both closures; compare echo phase mismatch and 100-period unforced energy drift against acceptance thresholds.
EchoJoint-v1 audit: 32-pole had 8.8% echo error, 0.04-rad phase error, and 0.06% energy drift; 64-mode phase error reached 0.16 rad.
Does coupled 32-pole memory maintain ≤10% echo error for unseen 24–32-period delays at k₂/k₁=2.5?
Extend EchoJoint-v1’s audited 32-pole baseline to 24–32-period delays at k₂/k₁=2.5; compare echo error and 100-period unforced energy drift.
At 32-period delay and k₂/k₁=2.5, coupled 32-pole echo error reached 16.3%; unforced 100-period energy drift remained 0.07%.
Prioritize coupled 32-pole over 64-mode for mixed histories, but expand memory to address 16.3% long-delay echo error.
Expand port-Hamiltonian memory to 64 antisymmetrically coupled poles, retaining discrete-gradient stepping for long-delay echoes and unforced energy conservation.
Will 64 coupled poles resolve the 32-period, k₂/k₁=2.5 echo deficit without exceeding 0.1% unforced energy drift?
Expanding to 64 coupled poles will reduce 32-period, k₂/k₁=2.5 echo error below 10%, retaining <0.1% unforced 100-period drift.
Following the 32-pole long-delay failure, fit 64 coupled poles; retest 24–32-period echoes and 100-period unforced energy drift.
Use EchoK-v1’s per-ratio error table to allocate 64 antisymmetrically coupled poles, then fit on separate training trajectories.
Coupled64-v1 checkpoint containing fitted 64-pole weights, EchoK-v1-guided pole allocation, antisymmetric coupling matrices, and discrete-gradient solver configuration.
Run Coupled64-v1 on the 24–32-period, k₂/k₁=2.5 challenge; compare echo error with 16.3% baseline and unforced energy drift.
Coupled64-v1 cut 32-period, k₂/k₁=2.5 echo error from 16.3% to 8.4%; unforced drift was 0.08% over 100 periods.
Does Coupled64-v1 maintain ≤10% echo error under unseen four-pulse chirped drives with randomized wavevectors and <0.1% unforced energy drift?
After 32-pole prioritization and long-delay success, benchmark Coupled64-v1 on 200 unseen four-pulse chirps against Vlasov–Poisson echoes; check 100-period unforced drift.
Across 200 unseen four-pulse chirps, Coupled64-v1’s maximum echo error was 9.2%; 100-period unforced energy drift was 0.09%.
Select Coupled64-v1 over initially promising 64-mode Hermite and prioritized 32-pole memory; long-delay and four-pulse tests meet both thresholds.
